units.source_text: Doxorubicin is given intravenously on day 1 by trained staff through suitable venous access. Blood tests, review, anti-sickness medicines and observation make the whole visit longer than the injection itself.

units.source_text: Confirm the full three-day treatment and post-treatment mesna/fluid plan, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (white-cell growth support) (G-CSF) injections, stomach protection and anti-sickness medicines before starting. Tell the team about sedating medicines or new confusion. Do not change fluid intake or medicines without the team’s advice.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Each treatment day includes intravenous doxorubicin followed by a 3-hour ifosfamide infusion, with prescribed mesna and fluids. Mesna includes a prolonged infusion and hydration continues after chemotherapy; the service confirms admission, pump arrangements and the actual finish time.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC), agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements. Confirm who manages the mesna pump and when it is disconnected; do not alter pump settings yourself.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential bladder protection. NCCP requires G-CSF support and proton-pump inhibitor prophylaxis for this regimen; the team specifies product, dose and timing. Multi-day anti-sickness treatment needs a single reconciled prescription. Aprepitant may increase ifosfamide-related brain toxicity, so pharmacy must check the chosen plan.

units.source_text: Get the day 7–9 dexamethasone prescription before the day 8 visit. Contact the team if doses were missed or vomited; do not silently double doses. Review diabetes control, infection symptoms and all medicines. Reconcile steroid premedication with any anti-sickness steroids.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Gemcitabine is infused over 90 minutes on both days 1 and 8. On day 8 it is followed by docetaxel over 60 minutes. Allow additional time for blood tests, review, line care and observation.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC), agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements.

units.source_text: Take dexamethasone 8 mg by mouth twice daily for 3 days, starting day 7, unless your team prescribes an explicitly revised plan; NCCP requires at least 3 doses before docetaxel. This reduces allergic reactions and fluid retention. Both drugs have low emetogenic classification in this source. granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (white-cell growth support) (G-CSF) may be used based on the prescribed risk plan; it is not mandatory for every patient in NCCP 00501.
